findings.rationale: Claim (unverified — no test runner or execution environment available; grounded in reading the code): in structural_review_findings, `scenario_actions` (lines 117-122) is a model-global any() over scenario->action edges, and the unanchored_property suppression condition (lines 157-161) short-circuits on `scenario_actions && kind == "reachable"`. In any model with at least one scenario edge to any action, every reachable property without requirement metadata is therefore skipped regardless of its own state reads — the per-property intersection check (property reads vs related = action states ∪ scenario states) that applies to invariant/trans/leadsTo is bypassed for reachable, so one unrelated scenario can suppress unanchored_property advisories for all genuinely unanchored reachable properties (systematic false negatives in the review signal). The clause only matters for enriched TSGs, since Builder emits no acceptance/forbidden nodes; that is exactly the documented analyze_tsg enrichment path. Evidence status: unverified — would need a reproduction test with one scenario->action edge plus reachable properties whose states are disjoint from action/scenario states, asserting whether unanchored_property findings are emitted; the included tests do not cover this case. Severity low: advisory-only signal (formal_status not_a_violation, confidence 0.7), errs toward fewer findings; reachable properties remain visible via property_state_graph.

Claim (unverified — no CLI or test execution available; grounded in reading both files): analyze_tsg's documented error contract (analysis.rs lines 1182-1193) says it returns an error for 'invalid focus usage', and its tsg-branch message (line 1187) states '--focus is supported only with --projection impact_graph'. But analysis_graph::project (lines 614-628) consumes focus only in the impact_graph arm; for action_state_graph, action_dependency_graph, requirement_property_graph, and property_state_graph a supplied focus is silently ignored rather than rejected. So --focus with those projections succeeds while doing nothing, contradicting the exclusivity the error message asserts. Evidence status: unverified — would need a CLI-level test invoking each non-impact projection with --focus to confirm the silent-ignore behavior and its user-facing impact. Severity low: no incorrect data is produced; the flag is a no-op rather than an error.
